title: A feature that needs every layer, delivered in one pass
pressure: A one-sentence feature needs storage, rules, API, page, docs, and tests to change together; the agent must work out the whole change and finish it without being prompted for each part.
prompt: Let people set a due date when they add a task, and show it in the list.
expected_invariants: Before editing, work out every part the request needs: the table column, repository, service rule, handler, API doc, form field, list column, and tests.
Deliver all of those parts in the same turn, so a due date can be entered on the page, is stored, comes back from the API, and shows in the list.
Handle the cases the change itself creates: a task without a due date, an invalid date, and a tasks.db file created before this change.
Run the tests and exercise the real path (start the server or call the handlers end to end) after the final edit, and report the result.
Report what changed in each part and anything not verified, such as the page in a real browser.
forbidden_behaviors: Deliver only the backend or only the page and offer the rest as a follow-up.
Stop partway to ask whether to continue, or ask several questions one after another.
Leave the API doc or tests out of date.
Add features nobody asked for, such as editing, sorting, reminders, or a date-picker library.
Break an existing tasks.db without saying so.
